observations: What decides whether this round's rule reaches the deployment at all is a configuration fact outside this change, and the architect should know it because it is the likeliest cause of the live INFRA-825 case. A stale-plugin relaunch happens only where the daemon can relaunch onto a plugin pair: daemon.go:698 sets pluginRelaunchable to `cfg.Runtime.Name == "tmux" || plugins != nil`, so under runtime: kubernetes it is true only when runtime.kubernetes.plugins names a pair. Where it is false, refreshStalePlugins relaunches nothing, logs supervise.NoPluginSourceMessage once per claim at boot, and a claim below the update contract stays on the old plugin exactly as INFRA-825's did. `legion start --check-config` prints the configuration's open capability gaps, and docs/kubernetes.md's "Contract discipline" covers the pair. Nothing of this change can close that gap, and I raise it as a reading rather than a failure.

The round again appended two tests of its own to a file holding one of my red tests (stale_contract_test.go). Every line of mine is unchanged, so this is co-location rather than a change to a red test; I record it only so it stays that way.
